skill.name: performance-fundamentals
skill.description: Guides reviews of application performance in loops, data fetching, rendering, database access, API payloads, memory cleanup, and resource-heavy operations.

content.value_statement: Performance bugs often hide in normal code reviews until traffic or data volume grows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused checklist for finding common scalability issues.
actual_capabilities: Reviews database access for N+1 queries, missing indexes, pagination gaps, and excessive field selection.
Checks frontend rendering patterns for avoidable re-renders, expensive render work, and missing memoization.
Evaluates API responses for oversized payloads, missing compression, weak caching, and slow synchronous work.
Highlights resource cleanup risks such as timers, subscriptions, listeners, and connection handling.
Uses scale-focused questions to guide junior developers toward performance-aware decisions.
Provides quick Big O references and target metrics for common web performance reviews.
limitations: Does not run benchmarks, load tests, profilers, or database explain plans by itself.
Cannot prove performance impact without runtime data from the target application.
May need framework-specific context to judge memoization, caching, and query strategies correctly.
Focuses on common review patterns, not deep systems tuning or infrastructure capacity planning.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests for Scalability
use_cases.description: Find common performance risks in changed code before the branch is merged.

use_cases.title: Coach Junior Developers
use_cases.description: Use targeted questions to teach query count, rendering cost, memory cleanup, and payload size.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Readiness Checks
use_cases.description: Review endpoints, data flows, and UI paths for issues that appear under larger data sets.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Performance Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a small pull request or focused code snippet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for basic performance issues. Focus on loops, queries, rendering, payload size, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Database and API Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the change touches endpoints, queries, or returned data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the database and API performance of this change. Check query count, indexes, pagination, selected fields, caching headers, and response size.

prompt_templates.title: Frontend Render Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for React, Vue, or similar UI component changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI code for rendering performance. Look for expensive render work, unnecessary re-renders, missing memoization, large lists, and missing cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Scalability Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before shipping a high-traffic workflow or large-data feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for scalability risks. Estimate behavior at 10,000 and 1,000,000 records, identify bottlenecks, and suggest measurable validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a list endpoint that returns every user with all related records.
output: The endpoint may create large responses and slow database work as the user table grows.
Add pagination, select only needed fields, and fetch related records in a bounded query.
Measure response time and payload size at realistic record counts.

output_examples.input: Review a UI component that sorts data and creates callbacks during every render.
output: Sorting during render can repeat expensive work after unrelated state changes.
Move derived data into memoized computation and keep callback identities stable when child renders matter.
Confirm the change with component render counts or browser profiling.

output_examples.input: Review an effect that starts polling but has no cleanup path.
output: The polling task can continue after the component unmounts and waste client resources.
Return a cleanup function that clears the timer or cancels the active request.
Check for duplicate polling when users navigate away and back.

best_practices: Review performance against expected data volume, not only the current sample size.
Pair each suggested optimization with a measurement plan or observable production metric.
Prefer clear fixes for query count, pagination, cleanup, and payload size before complex tuning.
anti_patterns: Treating every slow path as a memoization problem without checking data access first.
Optimizing small local examples while ignoring production record counts and traffic patterns.
Adding caches without invalidation rules, ownership, monitoring, or memory limits.

faq.question: Does this skill run performance benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. It guides code review and suggests measurements, but it does not execute benchmark or profiling tools.

faq.question: Can it find N+1 database queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts review of queries inside loops and recommends bulk loading or joined fetching when appropriate.

faq.question: Does it work for frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers render work, re-renders, memoization, image handling, bundle size, and cleanup concerns.

faq.question: Does it replace a senior performance review?
faq.answer: No. It is a structured checklist that helps reviewers find common issues and ask better questions.

faq.question: What inputs make it most useful?
faq.answer: Provide changed files, expected traffic, typical record counts, framework details, and any known latency targets.

faq.question: Can Codex and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.
